entries.title: Smooth Scroll
entries.summary: Anchor links should scroll smoothly to target section
entries.content:
No: 1
Category: Navigation
Issue: Smooth Scroll
Platform: Web
Description: Anchor links should scroll smoothly to target section
Do: Use scroll-behavior: smooth on html element
Don't: Jump directly without transition
Code Example Good: html { scroll-behavior: smooth; }
Code Example Bad: <a href='#section'> without CSS
Severity: High

entries.title: Loading States
entries.summary: Show feedback during async operations
entries.content:
No: 10
Category: Animation
Issue: Loading States
Platform: All
Description: Show feedback during async operations
Do: Use skeleton screens or spinners
Don't: Leave UI frozen with no feedback
Code Example Good: animate-pulse skeleton
Code Example Bad: Blank screen while loading
Severity: High

entries.title: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
entries.summary: WCAG 2.2 AA requires keyboard focus to remain at least partially visible
entries.content:
No: 100
Category: Accessibility
Issue: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
Platform: Web
Description: WCAG 2.2 AA requires keyboard focus to remain at least partially visible
Do: Offset sticky UI with scroll-padding and dismiss or move persistent overlays
Don't: Let headers footers banners or chat widgets fully cover focus
Code Example Good: scroll-padding-top: var(--header-height)
Code Example Bad: fixed overlay covers :focus
Severity: High

entries.title: Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced)
entries.summary: WCAG 2.2 AAA requires keyboard focus to remain fully visible
entries.content:
No: 101
Category: Accessibility
Issue: Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced)
Platform: Web
Description: WCAG 2.2 AAA requires keyboard focus to remain fully visible
Do: Keep the entire focused component unobscured by author-created content
Don't: Present this enhanced AAA criterion as an AA requirement or allow persistent UI to hide any part of focus
Code Example Good: close persistent overlay before focus moves behind it
Code Example Bad: sticky footer covers half the focused button
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Focus Appearance
entries.summary: WCAG 2.2 AAA defines minimum area and contrast for focus indicators
entries.content:
No: 102
Category: Accessibility
Issue: Focus Appearance
Platform: Web
Description: WCAG 2.2 AAA defines minimum area and contrast for focus indicators
Do: Use an indicator at least as large as a 2 CSS px perimeter with 3:1 state contrast
Don't: Present this enhanced AAA criterion as an AA requirement or use a thin low-contrast outline
Code Example Good: outline: 2px solid currentColor; outline-offset: 2px
Code Example Bad: box-shadow: 0 0 1px low-contrast
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Dragging Movements
entries.summary: WCAG 2.2 AA requires a single-pointer alternative for author-controlled drag operations
entries.content:
No: 103
Category: Accessibility
Issue: Dragging Movements
Platform: All
Description: WCAG 2.2 AA requires a single-pointer alternative for author-controlled drag operations
Do: Add buttons menus or tap-to-move controls and retain keyboard operation
Don't: Make dragging the only way to reorder resize or select
Code Example Good: Move up and Move down buttons beside drag handle
Code Example Bad: drag handle only
Severity: High

entries.title: Target Size (Minimum)
entries.summary: WCAG 2.2 AA requires 24 CSS px pointer targets or an applicable exception
entries.content:
No: 104
Category: Accessibility
Issue: Target Size (Minimum)
Platform: Web
Description: WCAG 2.2 AA requires 24 CSS px pointer targets or an applicable exception
Do: Use at least 24 by 24 CSS px or verify spacing equivalent inline user-agent or essential exceptions
Don't: Assume native 44pt or 48dp guidance defines web conformance
Code Example Good: min-width: 24px; min-height: 24px
Code Example Bad: tiny adjacent icon buttons
Severity: High

entries.title: Consistent Help
entries.summary: WCAG 2.2 A requires repeated help mechanisms to stay in the same relative order
entries.content:
No: 105
Category: Accessibility
Issue: Consistent Help
Platform: All
Description: WCAG 2.2 A requires repeated help mechanisms to stay in the same relative order
Do: Keep contact self-help and automated help in consistent locations
Don't: Move help controls to different locations on each page
Code Example Good: shared header help menu
Code Example Bad: page-specific help placement
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Redundant Entry
entries.summary: WCAG 2.2 A avoids requiring the same information twice in one process
entries.content:
No: 106
Category: Forms
Issue: Redundant Entry
Platform: All
Description: WCAG 2.2 A avoids requiring the same information twice in one process
Do: Auto-populate prior values or let users select previously entered information
Don't: Ask users to retype the same address or account data without necessity
Code Example Good: reuse confirmed shipping address
Code Example Bad: repeat full address form
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
entries.summary: WCAG 2.2 AA says authentication must not depend only on a cognitive function test unless an exception applies
entries.content:
No: 107
Category: Security / Accessibility
Issue: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
Platform: All
Description: WCAG 2.2 AA says authentication must not depend only on a cognitive function test unless an exception applies
Do: Allow password managers and paste; offer passkeys OAuth or another non-cognitive method
Don't: Block paste or require manual OTP transcription with no alternative
Code Example Good: autocomplete="current-password" and paste allowed
Code Example Bad: onpaste preventDefault
Severity: Critical

entries.title: Auto-Rotating Content Controls
entries.summary: Auto-rotating content needs user control
entries.content:
No: 108
Category: Animation
Issue: Auto-Rotating Content Controls
Platform: All
Description: Auto-rotating content needs user control
Do: Provide previous next and play/pause; stop on focus or hover and when reduced motion is requested
Don't: Auto-advance slides without a stop control
Code Example Good: button aria-label="Pause carousel"
Code Example Bad: timer-only carousel
Severity: High

entries.title: Focusable Error Summary
entries.summary: An error summary for failed validation complements inline field errors and must be easy to find by keyboard and screen reader users
entries.content:
No: 109 Category: Forms / Accessibility Issue: Focusable Error Summary Platform: Web Description: An error summary for failed validation complements inline field errors and must be easy to find by keyboard and screen reader users Do: Place it at the top of the form; move focus to its heading or container after failed submit; link each item to its invalid field; retain inline errors Don't: Replace inline errors with a visual-only summary or move focus on every blur Code Example Good:

There is a problem

Enter an email address
Code Example Bad: Toast only with no field links or focus target Severity: High

entries.title: Hover vs Tap
entries.summary: Hover effects don't work on touch devices
entries.content:
No: 11
Category: Animation
Issue: Hover vs Tap
Platform: All
Description: Hover effects don't work on touch devices
Do: Use click/tap for primary interactions
Don't: Rely only on hover for important actions
Code Example Good: onClick handler
Code Example Bad: onMouseEnter only
Severity: High

entries.title: Heading Line Balance
entries.summary: Short multi-line headings may use balanced wrapping as a progressive visual heuristic
entries.content:
No: 110
Category: Typography
Issue: Heading Line Balance
Platform: Web
Description: Short multi-line headings may use balanced wrapping as a progressive visual heuristic
Do: Bound the measure and test natural-wrap fallback across widths fonts and locales
Don't: Promise an exact final line or insert blanket nonbreaking spaces or hardcoded br tags
Code Example Good: .hero-title { max-inline-size: 20ch; text-wrap: balance; }
Code Example Bad: Heading copy rewritten with forced last-line breaks
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Long Token Wrapping
entries.summary: URLs identifiers and user content must not force horizontal overflow
entries.content:
No: 111
Category: Layout
Issue: Long Token Wrapping
Platform: Web
Description: URLs identifiers and user content must not force horizontal overflow
Do: Use overflow-wrap anywhere and let flex or grid text children shrink
Don't: Apply word-break break-all to all prose
Code Example Good: .token { min-inline-size: 0; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
Code Example Bad: .token { white-space: nowrap; }
Severity: High

entries.title: Text Reflow and Spacing
entries.summary: Text must remain available at narrow widths zoom and user spacing overrides
entries.content:
No: 112
Category: Accessibility
Issue: Text Reflow and Spacing
Platform: Web
Description: Text must remain available at narrow widths zoom and user spacing overrides
Do: Use fluid sizes content-driven height and unitless line height
Don't: Clip text in fixed-width or fixed-height boxes
Code Example Good: .copy { inline-size: min(100%, 65ch); height: auto; line-height: 1.5; }
Code Example Bad: .copy { width: 900px; height: 40px; overflow: hidden; }
Severity: Critical

entries.title: Essential Text Truncation
entries.summary: Headings actions errors safety text and distinguishing names need complete access
entries.content:
No: 113
Category: Content
Issue: Essential Text Truncation
Platform: All
Description: Headings actions errors safety text and distinguishing names need complete access
Do: Wrap stack resize or provide a visible full-detail path
Don't: Clamp essential meaning only to make cards uniform
Code Example Good: Action label wraps or opens full details
Code Example Bad: Primary action shown only as an unexplained ellipsis
Severity: Critical

entries.title: Compact Label Semantics
entries.summary: Badges communicate state while chips or tags represent values or actions
entries.content:
No: 114 Category: Content Issue: Compact Label Semantics Platform: All Description: Badges communicate state while chips or tags represent values or actions Do: Choose static or interactive markup from the label's meaning and ownership Don't: Make every pill clickable or encode status with color alone Code Example Good: Pending Code Example Bad:
Pending
Severity: High

entries.title: Chip Collection Reflow
entries.summary: Filter chips and editable value collections must preserve labels when space or text size changes
entries.content:
No: 115 Category: Layout Issue: Chip Collection Reflow Platform: All Description: Filter chips and editable value collections must preserve labels when space or text size changes Do: Wrap the collection or use an operable +n disclosure for hidden overflow values Don't: Force all chips into one clipped row or hide overflow values Code Example Good:
{chips}
with flex-wrap Code Example Bad:
Severity: High

entries.title: Compact Label Overflow
entries.summary: A badge chip or pill label should stay whole on one line when practical and disclose unavoidable truncation
entries.content:
No: 116
Category: Content
Issue: Compact Label Overflow
Platform: All
Description: A badge chip or pill label should stay whole on one line when practical and disclose unavoidable truncation
Do: Bound only unpredictable values; use nowrap with a shrinkable label; expose full text to keyboard pointer and touch users
Don't: Let one compact label wrap to a second line or use a hover-only tooltip
Code Example Good: Flexible label with min-width 0 and an operable full-value disclosure
Code Example Bad: Fixed-width badge wraps to second line or clips with title-only recovery
Severity: High

entries.title: Compact Control Semantics
entries.summary: Interactive chips need a native role accessible name state keyboard operation and visible focus
entries.content:
No: 117 Category: Accessibility Issue: Compact Control Semantics Platform: Web Description: Interactive chips need a native role accessible name state keyboard operation and visible focus Do: Prefer a button and expose pressed or selected state that matches the visible label Don't: Use a clickable div or reveal the only action on hover Code Example Good: Code Example Bad:
Open now
Severity: Critical

entries.title: Contextual Live Badge Updates
entries.summary: Async badge and count changes should announce a meaningful contextual status without moving focus
entries.content: No: 118 Category: Accessibility Issue: Contextual Live Badge Updates Platform: Web Description: Async badge and count changes should announce a meaningful contextual status without moving focus Do: Use one appropriate atomic status message such as 3 items in cart Don't: Announce a bare number or make every badge a competing live region Code Example Good: 3 items in cart Code Example Bad: 3 Severity: High

entries.title: Cancellable State Transitions
entries.summary: Rapid compact-control changes can interrupt an in-flight transition
entries.content:
No: 119
Category: Animation
Issue: Cancellable State Transitions
Platform: Web
Description: Rapid compact-control changes can interrupt an in-flight transition
Do: Cancel or replace prior motion; set the final semantic state directly and handle cancellation cleanup
Don't: Depend on animationend or transitionend for required state correctness
Code Example Good: previous?.cancel(); setSelected(next)
Code Example Bad: Enable the chip only inside transitionend
Severity: High

entries.title: Continuous Animation
entries.summary: Infinite animations are distracting
entries.content:
No: 12
Category: Animation
Issue: Continuous Animation
Platform: All
Description: Infinite animations are distracting
Do: Use for loading indicators only
Don't: Use for decorative elements
Code Example Good: animate-spin on loader
Code Example Bad: animate-bounce on icons
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Transform Performance
entries.summary: Some CSS properties trigger expensive repaints
entries.content:
No: 13
Category: Animation
Issue: Transform Performance
Platform: Web
Description: Some CSS properties trigger expensive repaints
Do: Use transform and opacity for animations
Don't: Animate width/height/top/left properties
Code Example Good: transform: translateY()
Code Example Bad: top: 10px animation
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Easing Functions
entries.summary: Easing should match how an element changes speed and purpose
entries.content:
No: 14
Category: Animation
Issue: Easing Functions
Platform: All
Description: Easing should match how an element changes speed and purpose
Do: Use deceleration when arriving acceleration when leaving and linear for constant-rate progress
Don't: Reject linear easing even for steady rotation or progress
Code Example Good: ease-out for entry; linear for spinner
Code Example Bad: ease-in-out for every motion
Severity: Low

entries.title: Z-Index Management
entries.summary: Stacking context conflicts cause hidden elements
entries.content:
No: 15
Category: Layout
Issue: Z-Index Management
Platform: Web
Description: Stacking context conflicts cause hidden elements
Do: Define z-index scale system (10 20 30 50)
Don't: Use arbitrary large z-index values
Code Example Good: z-10 z-20 z-50
Code Example Bad: z-[9999]
Severity: High

entries.title: Overflow Hidden
entries.summary: Hidden overflow can clip important content
entries.content:
No: 16
Category: Layout
Issue: Overflow Hidden
Platform: Web
Description: Hidden overflow can clip important content
Do: Test all content fits within containers
Don't: Blindly apply overflow-hidden
Code Example Good: overflow-auto with scroll
Code Example Bad: overflow-hidden truncating content
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Fixed Positioning
entries.summary: Fixed elements can overlap or be inaccessible
entries.content:
No: 17
Category: Layout
Issue: Fixed Positioning
Platform: Web
Description: Fixed elements can overlap or be inaccessible
Do: Account for safe areas and other fixed elements
Don't: Stack multiple fixed elements carelessly
Code Example Good: Fixed nav + fixed bottom with gap
Code Example Bad: Multiple overlapping fixed elements
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Stacking Context
entries.summary: New stacking contexts reset z-index
entries.content:
No: 18
Category: Layout
Issue: Stacking Context
Platform: Web
Description: New stacking contexts reset z-index
Do: Understand what creates new stacking context
Don't: Expect z-index to work across contexts
Code Example Good: Parent with z-index isolates children
Code Example Bad: z-index: 9999 not working
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Content Jumping
entries.summary: Images badges validation text and skeleton replacements can shift nearby content when they update
entries.content:
No: 19
Category: Layout
Issue: Content Jumping
Platform: Web
Description: Images badges validation text and skeleton replacements can shift nearby content when they update
Do: Reserve appropriate space or keep async states in a stable content-driven container
Don't: Insert compact text or media without a layout strategy
Code Example Good: aspect-ratio for media; stable count slot for badges
Code Example Bad: Badge insertion pushes toolbar actions
Severity: High

entries.title: Sticky Navigation
entries.summary: Fixed nav should not obscure content
entries.content:
No: 2
Category: Navigation
Issue: Sticky Navigation
Platform: Web
Description: Fixed nav should not obscure content
Do: Add padding-top to body equal to nav height
Don't: Let nav overlap first section content
Code Example Good: pt-20 (if nav is h-20)
Code Example Bad: No padding compensation
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Viewport Units
entries.summary: 100vh can be problematic on mobile browsers
entries.content:
No: 20
Category: Layout
Issue: Viewport Units
Platform: Web
Description: 100vh can be problematic on mobile browsers
Do: Use dvh or account for mobile browser chrome
Don't: Use 100vh for full-screen mobile layouts
Code Example Good: min-h-dvh or min-h-screen
Code Example Bad: h-screen on mobile
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Container Width
entries.summary: Content too wide is hard to read
entries.content:
No: 21
Category: Layout
Issue: Container Width
Platform: Web
Description: Content too wide is hard to read
Do: Limit max-width for text content (65-75ch)
Don't: Let text span full viewport width
Code Example Good: max-w-prose or max-w-3xl
Code Example Bad: Full width paragraphs
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Touch Target Size
entries.summary: Touch target guidance depends on platform and web context
entries.content:
No: 22
Category: Touch
Issue: Touch Target Size
Platform: Mobile
Description: Touch target guidance depends on platform and web context
Do: Use 44pt on iOS and 48dp on Android; for web use the separate WCAG Target Size rule
Don't: Treat one unit or minimum as universal across platforms
Code Example Good: iOS 44pt; Android 48dp; Web 24 CSS px plus WCAG exceptions
Code Example Bad: w-6 h-6 buttons
Severity: High

entries.title: Touch Spacing
entries.summary: Adjacent touch targets need adequate spacing
entries.content:
No: 23
Category: Touch
Issue: Touch Spacing
Platform: Mobile
Description: Adjacent touch targets need adequate spacing
Do: Minimum 8px gap between touch targets
Don't: Tightly packed clickable elements
Code Example Good: gap-2 between buttons
Code Example Bad: gap-0 or gap-1
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Gesture Conflicts
entries.summary: Custom gestures can conflict with system
entries.content:
No: 24
Category: Touch
Issue: Gesture Conflicts
Platform: Mobile
Description: Custom gestures can conflict with system
Do: Avoid horizontal swipe on main content
Don't: Override system gestures
Code Example Good: Vertical scroll primary
Code Example Bad: Horizontal swipe carousel only
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Tap Delay
entries.summary: 300ms tap delay feels laggy
entries.content:
No: 25
Category: Touch
Issue: Tap Delay
Platform: Mobile
Description: 300ms tap delay feels laggy
Do: Use touch-action CSS or fastclick
Don't: Default mobile tap handling
Code Example Good: touch-action: manipulation
Code Example Bad: No touch optimization
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Pull to Refresh
entries.summary: Accidental refresh is frustrating
entries.content:
No: 26
Category: Touch
Issue: Pull to Refresh
Platform: Mobile
Description: Accidental refresh is frustrating
Do: Disable where not needed
Don't: Enable by default everywhere
Code Example Good: overscroll-behavior: contain
Code Example Bad: Default overscroll
Severity: Low

entries.title: Haptic Feedback
entries.summary: Tactile feedback improves interaction feel
entries.content:
No: 27
Category: Touch
Issue: Haptic Feedback
Platform: Mobile
Description: Tactile feedback improves interaction feel
Do: Use for confirmations and important actions
Don't: Overuse vibration feedback
Code Example Good: navigator.vibrate(10)
Code Example Bad: Vibrate on every tap
Severity: Low

entries.title: Focus States
entries.summary: Keyboard focus, including controls inside a modal, needs a visible indicator
entries.content:
No: 28
Category: Interaction
Issue: Focus States
Platform: All
Description: Keyboard focus, including controls inside a modal, needs a visible indicator
Do: Use a visible focus ring on every interactive control, including modal controls
Don't: Remove focus outline without replacement
Code Example Good: focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500
Code Example Bad: outline-none without alternative
Severity: High

entries.title: Hover States
entries.summary: Visual feedback on interactive elements
entries.content:
No: 29
Category: Interaction
Issue: Hover States
Platform: Web
Description: Visual feedback on interactive elements
Do: Change cursor and add subtle visual change
Don't: No hover feedback on clickable elements
Code Example Good: hover:bg-gray-100 cursor-pointer
Code Example Bad: No hover style
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Active State
entries.summary: Current page/section should be visually indicated
entries.content:
No: 3
Category: Navigation
Issue: Active State
Platform: All
Description: Current page/section should be visually indicated
Do: Highlight active nav item with color/underline
Don't: No visual feedback on current location
Code Example Good: text-primary border-b-2
Code Example Bad: All links same style
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Active States
entries.summary: Show immediate feedback on press/click
entries.content:
No: 30
Category: Interaction
Issue: Active States
Platform: All
Description: Show immediate feedback on press/click
Do: Add pressed/active state visual change
Don't: No feedback during interaction
Code Example Good: active:scale-95
Code Example Bad: No active state
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Disabled States
entries.summary: Clearly indicate non-interactive elements
entries.content:
No: 31
Category: Interaction
Issue: Disabled States
Platform: All
Description: Clearly indicate non-interactive elements
Do: Reduce opacity and change cursor
Don't: Confuse disabled with normal state
Code Example Good: opacity-50 cursor-not-allowed
Code Example Bad: Same style as enabled
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Loading Buttons
entries.summary: Prevent double submission during async actions
entries.content:
No: 32
Category: Interaction
Issue: Loading Buttons
Platform: All
Description: Prevent double submission during async actions
Do: Disable button and show loading state
Don't: Allow multiple clicks during processing
Code Example Good: disabled={loading} spinner
Code Example Bad: Button clickable while loading
Severity: High

entries.title: Error Feedback
entries.summary: Users need to know when something fails
entries.content:
No: 33
Category: Interaction
Issue: Error Feedback
Platform: All
Description: Users need to know when something fails
Do: Show clear error messages near problem
Don't: Silent failures with no feedback
Code Example Good: Red border + error message
Code Example Bad: No indication of error
Severity: High

entries.title: Success Feedback
entries.summary: Confirm successful actions to users
entries.content:
No: 34
Category: Interaction
Issue: Success Feedback
Platform: All
Description: Confirm successful actions to users
Do: Show success message or visual change
Don't: No confirmation of completed action
Code Example Good: Toast notification or checkmark
Code Example Bad: Action completes silently
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Confirmation Dialogs
entries.summary: Prevent accidental destructive actions
entries.content:
No: 35
Category: Interaction
Issue: Confirmation Dialogs
Platform: All
Description: Prevent accidental destructive actions
Do: Confirm before delete/irreversible actions
Don't: Delete without confirmation
Code Example Good: Are you sure modal
Code Example Bad: Direct delete on click
Severity: High

entries.title: Color Contrast
entries.summary: Text must be readable against background
entries.content:
No: 36
Category: Accessibility
Issue: Color Contrast
Platform: All
Description: Text must be readable against background
Do: Minimum 4.5:1 ratio for normal text
Don't: Low contrast text
Code Example Good: #333 on white (7:1)
Code Example Bad: #999 on white (2.8:1)
Severity: High

entries.title: Color Only
entries.summary: Don't convey information by color alone
entries.content:
No: 37
Category: Accessibility
Issue: Color Only
Platform: All
Description: Don't convey information by color alone
Do: Use icons/text in addition to color
Don't: Red/green only for error/success
Code Example Good: Red text + error icon
Code Example Bad: Red border only for error
Severity: High

entries.title: Alt Text
entries.summary: Images need text alternatives
entries.content:
No: 38
Category: Accessibility
Issue: Alt Text
Platform: All
Description: Images need text alternatives
Do: Descriptive alt text for meaningful images
Don't: Empty or missing alt attributes
Code Example Good: alt='Dog playing in park'
Code Example Bad: alt='' for content images
Severity: High

entries.title: Heading Hierarchy
entries.summary: Screen readers use headings for navigation
entries.content:
No: 39
Category: Accessibility
Issue: Heading Hierarchy
Platform: Web
Description: Screen readers use headings for navigation
Do: Use sequential heading levels h1-h6
Don't: Skip heading levels or misuse for styling
Code Example Good: h1 then h2 then h3
Code Example Bad: h1 then h4
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Back Button
entries.summary: Users expect back to work predictably
entries.content:
No: 4
Category: Navigation
Issue: Back Button
Platform: Mobile
Description: Users expect back to work predictably
Do: Preserve navigation history properly
Don't: Break browser/app back button behavior
Code Example Good: history.pushState()
Code Example Bad: location.replace()
Severity: High

entries.title: ARIA Labels
entries.summary: Interactive elements need accessible names
entries.content:
No: 40
Category: Accessibility
Issue: ARIA Labels
Platform: All
Description: Interactive elements need accessible names
Do: Add aria-label for icon-only buttons
Don't: Icon buttons without labels
Code Example Good: aria-label='Close menu'
Code Example Bad: <button><Icon/></button>
Severity: High

entries.title: Keyboard Navigation
entries.summary: Web users need complete keyboard navigation with visible focus on every operable control
entries.content:
No: 41
Category: Accessibility
Issue: Keyboard Navigation
Platform: Web
Description: Web users need complete keyboard navigation with visible focus on every operable control
Do: Keep tab order aligned with visual order and test every action without a pointer
Don't: Keyboard traps or illogical tab order
Code Example Good: tabIndex for custom order
Code Example Bad: Unreachable elements
Severity: High

entries.title: Screen Reader
entries.summary: Content should make sense when read aloud
entries.content:
No: 42
Category: Accessibility
Issue: Screen Reader
Platform: All
Description: Content should make sense when read aloud
Do: Use semantic HTML and ARIA properly
Don't: Div soup with no semantics
Code Example Good: <nav> <main> <article>
Code Example Bad: <div> for everything
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Form Labels
entries.summary: Inputs must have associated labels
entries.content:
No: 43
Category: Accessibility
Issue: Form Labels
Platform: All
Description: Inputs must have associated labels
Do: Use label with for attribute or wrap input
Don't: Placeholder-only inputs
Code Example Good: <label for='email'>
Code Example Bad: placeholder='Email' only
Severity: High

entries.title: Error Messages
entries.summary: Error messages must be announced
entries.content:
No: 44
Category: Accessibility
Issue: Error Messages
Platform: All
Description: Error messages must be announced
Do: Use aria-live or role=alert for errors
Don't: Visual-only error indication
Code Example Good: role='alert'
Code Example Bad: Red border only
Severity: High

entries.title: Skip Links
entries.summary: Allow keyboard users to skip navigation
entries.content:
No: 45
Category: Accessibility
Issue: Skip Links
Platform: Web
Description: Allow keyboard users to skip navigation
Do: Provide skip to main content link
Don't: No skip link on nav-heavy pages
Code Example Good: Skip to main content link
Code Example Bad: 100 tabs to reach content
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Image Optimization
entries.summary: Large images slow page load
entries.content:
No: 46
Category: Performance
Issue: Image Optimization
Platform: All
Description: Large images slow page load
Do: Use appropriate size and format (WebP)
Don't: Unoptimized full-size images
Code Example Good: srcset with multiple sizes
Code Example Bad: 4000px image for 400px display
Severity: High

entries.title: Lazy Loading
entries.summary: Load content as needed
entries.content:
No: 47
Category: Performance
Issue: Lazy Loading
Platform: All
Description: Load content as needed
Do: Lazy load below-fold images and content
Don't: Load everything upfront
Code Example Good: loading='lazy'
Code Example Bad: All images eager load
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Code Splitting
entries.summary: Large bundles slow initial load
entries.content:
No: 48
Category: Performance
Issue: Code Splitting
Platform: Web
Description: Large bundles slow initial load
Do: Split code by route/feature
Don't: Single large bundle
Code Example Good: dynamic import()
Code Example Bad: All code in main bundle
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Caching
entries.summary: Repeat visits should be fast
entries.content:
No: 49
Category: Performance
Issue: Caching
Platform: Web
Description: Repeat visits should be fast
Do: Set appropriate cache headers
Don't: No caching strategy
Code Example Good: Cache-Control headers
Code Example Bad: Every request hits server
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Deep Linking
entries.summary: URLs should reflect current state for sharing
entries.content:
No: 5
Category: Navigation
Issue: Deep Linking
Platform: All
Description: URLs should reflect current state for sharing
Do: Update URL on state/view changes
Don't: Static URLs for dynamic content
Code Example Good: Use query params or hash
Code Example Bad: Single URL for all states
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Font Loading
entries.summary: Web fonts can block rendering
entries.content:
No: 50
Category: Performance
Issue: Font Loading
Platform: Web
Description: Web fonts can block rendering
Do: Use font-display swap or optional
Don't: Invisible text during font load
Code Example Good: font-display: swap
Code Example Bad: FOIT (Flash of Invisible Text)
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Third Party Scripts
entries.summary: External scripts can block rendering
entries.content:
No: 51
Category: Performance
Issue: Third Party Scripts
Platform: Web
Description: External scripts can block rendering
Do: Load non-critical scripts async/defer
Don't: Synchronous third-party scripts
Code Example Good: async or defer attribute
Code Example Bad: <script src='...'> in head
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Bundle Size
entries.summary: Large JavaScript slows interaction
entries.content:
No: 52
Category: Performance
Issue: Bundle Size
Platform: Web
Description: Large JavaScript slows interaction
Do: Monitor and minimize bundle size
Don't: Ignore bundle size growth
Code Example Good: Bundle analyzer
Code Example Bad: No size monitoring
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Render Blocking
entries.summary: CSS/JS can block first paint
entries.content:
No: 53
Category: Performance
Issue: Render Blocking
Platform: Web
Description: CSS/JS can block first paint
Do: Inline critical CSS defer non-critical
Don't: Large blocking CSS files
Code Example Good: Critical CSS inline
Code Example Bad: All CSS in head
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Input Labels
entries.summary: Every input needs a visible label
entries.content:
No: 54
Category: Forms
Issue: Input Labels
Platform: All
Description: Every input needs a visible label
Do: Always show label above or beside input
Don't: Placeholder as only label
Code Example Good: <label>Email</label><input>
Code Example Bad: placeholder='Email' only
Severity: High

entries.title: Error Placement
entries.summary: Each invalid field needs an inline error connected to that field
entries.content:
No: 55 Category: Forms Issue: Error Placement Platform: All Description: Each invalid field needs an inline error connected to that field Do: Show a specific error below the input and reference it with aria-describedby Don't: Show only a top-level error without identifying each invalid field Code Example Good:

Enter an email address

Code Example Bad: Red border or summary only Severity: High

entries.title: Inline Validation
entries.summary: Validate as user types or on blur
entries.content:
No: 56
Category: Forms
Issue: Inline Validation
Platform: All
Description: Validate as user types or on blur
Do: Validate on blur for most fields
Don't: Validate only on submit
Code Example Good: onBlur validation
Code Example Bad: Submit-only validation
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Input Types
entries.summary: Use appropriate input types
entries.content:
No: 57
Category: Forms
Issue: Input Types
Platform: All
Description: Use appropriate input types
Do: Use email tel number url etc
Don't: Text input for everything
Code Example Good: type='email'
Code Example Bad: type='text' for email
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Autofill Support
entries.summary: Help browsers autofill correctly
entries.content:
No: 58
Category: Forms
Issue: Autofill Support
Platform: Web
Description: Help browsers autofill correctly
Do: Use autocomplete attribute properly
Don't: Block or ignore autofill
Code Example Good: autocomplete='email'
Code Example Bad: autocomplete='off' everywhere
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Required Indicators
entries.summary: Mark required fields clearly
entries.content:
No: 59
Category: Forms
Issue: Required Indicators
Platform: All
Description: Mark required fields clearly
Do: Use asterisk or (required) text
Don't: No indication of required fields
Code Example Good: * required indicator
Code Example Bad: Guess which are required
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Breadcrumbs
entries.summary: Show user location in site hierarchy
entries.content:
No: 6
Category: Navigation
Issue: Breadcrumbs
Platform: Web
Description: Show user location in site hierarchy
Do: Use for sites with 3+ levels of depth
Don't: Use for flat single-level sites
Code Example Good: Home > Category > Product
Code Example Bad: Only on deep nested pages
Severity: Low

entries.title: Password Visibility
entries.summary: Let users see password while typing
entries.content:
No: 60
Category: Forms
Issue: Password Visibility
Platform: All
Description: Let users see password while typing
Do: Toggle to show/hide password
Don't: No visibility toggle
Code Example Good: Show/hide password button
Code Example Bad: Password always hidden
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Submit Feedback
entries.summary: Confirm form submission status
entries.content:
No: 61
Category: Forms
Issue: Submit Feedback
Platform: All
Description: Confirm form submission status
Do: Show loading then success/error state
Don't: No feedback after submit
Code Example Good: Loading -> Success message
Code Example Bad: Button click with no response
Severity: High

entries.title: Input Affordance
entries.summary: Inputs should look interactive
entries.content:
No: 62
Category: Forms
Issue: Input Affordance
Platform: All
Description: Inputs should look interactive
Do: Use distinct input styling
Don't: Inputs that look like plain text
Code Example Good: Border/background on inputs
Code Example Bad: Borderless inputs
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Mobile Keyboards
entries.summary: Show appropriate keyboard for input type
entries.content:
No: 63
Category: Forms
Issue: Mobile Keyboards
Platform: Mobile
Description: Show appropriate keyboard for input type
Do: Use inputmode attribute
Don't: Default keyboard for all inputs
Code Example Good: inputmode='numeric'
Code Example Bad: Text keyboard for numbers
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Mobile First
entries.summary: Design for mobile then enhance for larger
entries.content:
No: 64
Category: Responsive
Issue: Mobile First
Platform: Web
Description: Design for mobile then enhance for larger
Do: Start with mobile styles then add breakpoints
Don't: Desktop-first causing mobile issues
Code Example Good: Default mobile + md: lg: xl:
Code Example Bad: Desktop default + max-width queries
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Breakpoint Testing
entries.summary: Test at all common screen sizes
entries.content:
No: 65
Category: Responsive
Issue: Breakpoint Testing
Platform: Web
Description: Test at all common screen sizes
Do: Test at 320 375 414 768 1024 1440
Don't: Only test on your device
Code Example Good: Multiple device testing
Code Example Bad: Single device development
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Touch Friendly
entries.summary: Mobile layouts need touch-sized targets
entries.content:
No: 66
Category: Responsive
Issue: Touch Friendly
Platform: Web
Description: Mobile layouts need touch-sized targets
Do: Increase touch targets on mobile
Don't: Same tiny buttons on mobile
Code Example Good: Larger buttons on mobile
Code Example Bad: Desktop-sized targets on mobile
Severity: High

entries.title: Readable Font Size
entries.summary: Text must be readable on all devices
entries.content:
No: 67
Category: Responsive
Issue: Readable Font Size
Platform: All
Description: Text must be readable on all devices
Do: Minimum 16px body text on mobile
Don't: Tiny text on mobile
Code Example Good: text-base or larger
Code Example Bad: text-xs for body text
Severity: High

entries.title: Viewport Meta
entries.summary: Set viewport for mobile devices
entries.content:
No: 68
Category: Responsive
Issue: Viewport Meta
Platform: Web
Description: Set viewport for mobile devices
Do: Use width=device-width initial-scale=1
Don't: Missing or incorrect viewport
Code Example Good: <meta name='viewport'...>
Code Example Bad: No viewport meta tag
Severity: High

entries.title: Horizontal Scroll
entries.summary: Avoid horizontal scrolling
entries.content:
No: 69
Category: Responsive
Issue: Horizontal Scroll
Platform: Web
Description: Avoid horizontal scrolling
Do: Ensure content fits viewport width
Don't: Content wider than viewport
Code Example Good: max-w-full overflow-x-hidden
Code Example Bad: Horizontal scrollbar on mobile
Severity: High

entries.title: Excessive Motion
entries.summary: Too many animations cause distraction and motion sickness
entries.content:
No: 7
Category: Animation
Issue: Excessive Motion
Platform: All
Description: Too many animations cause distraction and motion sickness
Do: Animate 1-2 key elements per view maximum
Don't: Animate everything that moves
Code Example Good: Single hero animation
Code Example Bad: animate-bounce on 5+ elements
Severity: High

entries.title: Image Scaling
entries.summary: Images should scale with container
entries.content:
No: 70
Category: Responsive
Issue: Image Scaling
Platform: Web
Description: Images should scale with container
Do: Use max-width: 100% on images
Don't: Fixed width images overflow
Code Example Good: max-w-full h-auto
Code Example Bad: width='800' fixed
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Table Handling
entries.summary: Tables can overflow on mobile
entries.content:
No: 71
Category: Responsive
Issue: Table Handling
Platform: Web
Description: Tables can overflow on mobile
Do: Use horizontal scroll or card layout
Don't: Wide tables breaking layout
Code Example Good: overflow-x-auto wrapper
Code Example Bad: Table overflows viewport
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Line Height
entries.summary: Adequate line height improves readability
entries.content:
No: 72
Category: Typography
Issue: Line Height
Platform: All
Description: Adequate line height improves readability
Do: Use 1.5-1.75 for body text
Don't: Cramped or excessive line height
Code Example Good: leading-relaxed (1.625)
Code Example Bad: leading-none (1)
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Line Length
entries.summary: Long lines are hard to read
entries.content:
No: 73
Category: Typography
Issue: Line Length
Platform: Web
Description: Long lines are hard to read
Do: Limit to 65-75 characters per line
Don't: Full-width text on large screens
Code Example Good: max-w-prose
Code Example Bad: Full viewport width text
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Font Size Scale
entries.summary: Consistent type hierarchy aids scanning
entries.content:
No: 74
Category: Typography
Issue: Font Size Scale
Platform: All
Description: Consistent type hierarchy aids scanning
Do: Use consistent modular scale
Don't: Random font sizes
Code Example Good: Type scale (12 14 16 18 24 32)
Code Example Bad: Arbitrary sizes
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Font Loading
entries.summary: Fonts should load without layout shift
entries.content:
No: 75
Category: Typography
Issue: Font Loading
Platform: Web
Description: Fonts should load without layout shift
Do: Reserve space with fallback font
Don't: Layout shift when fonts load
Code Example Good: font-display: swap + similar fallback
Code Example Bad: No fallback font
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Contrast Readability
entries.summary: Body text needs good contrast
entries.content:
No: 76
Category: Typography
Issue: Contrast Readability
Platform: All
Description: Body text needs good contrast
Do: Use darker text on light backgrounds
Don't: Gray text on gray background
Code Example Good: text-gray-900 on white
Code Example Bad: text-gray-400 on gray-100
Severity: High

entries.title: Heading Clarity
entries.summary: Headings should stand out from body
entries.content:
No: 77
Category: Typography
Issue: Heading Clarity
Platform: All
Description: Headings should stand out from body
Do: Clear size/weight difference
Don't: Headings similar to body text
Code Example Good: Bold + larger size
Code Example Bad: Same size as body
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Loading Indicators
entries.summary: Loading feedback should match the expected wait and avoid flashing for near-instant work
entries.content:
No: 78
Category: Feedback
Issue: Loading Indicators
Platform: All
Description: Loading feedback should match the expected wait and avoid flashing for near-instant work
Do: Follow platform and component guidance; preserve layout focus and accessible busy status
Don't: Apply one timing threshold to every operation or leave long waits unexplained
Code Example Good: Stable skeleton or progress with aria-busy
Code Example Bad: Flickering spinner or frozen UI
Severity: High

entries.title: Empty States
entries.summary: Guide users when no content exists
entries.content:
No: 79
Category: Feedback
Issue: Empty States
Platform: All
Description: Guide users when no content exists
Do: Show helpful message and action
Don't: Blank empty screens
Code Example Good: No items yet. Create one!
Code Example Bad: Empty white space
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Duration Timing
entries.summary: Motion duration depends on distance complexity platform and user context
entries.content:
No: 8
Category: Animation
Issue: Duration Timing
Platform: All
Description: Motion duration depends on distance complexity platform and user context
Do: Use shared motion tokens and test that feedback stays responsive
Don't: Present 150-300ms or any cutoff as a universal requirement
Code Example Good: transition-colors duration-200
Code Example Bad: One duration copied to every transition
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Error Recovery
entries.summary: Help users recover from errors
entries.content:
No: 80
Category: Feedback
Issue: Error Recovery
Platform: All
Description: Help users recover from errors
Do: Provide clear next steps
Don't: Error without recovery path
Code Example Good: Try again button + help link
Code Example Bad: Error message only
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Progress Indicators
entries.summary: Show progress for multi-step processes
entries.content:
No: 81
Category: Feedback
Issue: Progress Indicators
Platform: All
Description: Show progress for multi-step processes
Do: Step indicators or progress bar
Don't: No indication of progress
Code Example Good: Step 2 of 4 indicator
Code Example Bad: No step information
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Toast Notifications
entries.summary: Transient messages for non-critical info
entries.content:
No: 82
Category: Feedback
Issue: Toast Notifications
Platform: All
Description: Transient messages for non-critical info
Do: Auto-dismiss after 3-5 seconds
Don't: Toasts that never disappear
Code Example Good: Auto-dismiss toast
Code Example Bad: Persistent toast
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Confirmation Messages
entries.summary: Confirm successful actions
entries.content:
No: 83
Category: Feedback
Issue: Confirmation Messages
Platform: All
Description: Confirm successful actions
Do: Brief success message
Don't: Silent success
Code Example Good: Saved successfully toast
Code Example Bad: No confirmation
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Truncation
entries.summary: Handle long content gracefully
entries.content:
No: 84
Category: Content
Issue: Truncation
Platform: All
Description: Handle long content gracefully
Do: Truncate with ellipsis and expand option
Don't: Overflow or broken layout
Code Example Good: line-clamp-2 with expand
Code Example Bad: Overflow or cut off
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Date Formatting
entries.summary: Use locale-appropriate date formats
entries.content:
No: 85
Category: Content
Issue: Date Formatting
Platform: All
Description: Use locale-appropriate date formats
Do: Use relative or locale-aware dates
Don't: Ambiguous date formats
Code Example Good: 2 hours ago or locale format
Code Example Bad: 01/02/03
Severity: Low

entries.title: Number Formatting
entries.summary: Format large numbers for readability
entries.content:
No: 86
Category: Content
Issue: Number Formatting
Platform: All
Description: Format large numbers for readability
Do: Use thousand separators or abbreviations
Don't: Long unformatted numbers
Code Example Good: 1.2K or 1,234
Code Example Bad: 1234567
Severity: Low

entries.title: Placeholder Content
entries.summary: Show realistic placeholders during dev
entries.content:
No: 87
Category: Content
Issue: Placeholder Content
Platform: All
Description: Show realistic placeholders during dev
Do: Use realistic sample data
Don't: Lorem ipsum everywhere
Code Example Good: Real sample content
Code Example Bad: Lorem ipsum
Severity: Low

entries.title: User Freedom
entries.summary: Users should be able to skip tutorials
entries.content:
No: 88
Category: Onboarding
Issue: User Freedom
Platform: All
Description: Users should be able to skip tutorials
Do: Provide Skip and Back buttons
Don't: Force linear unskippable tour
Code Example Good: Skip Tutorial button
Code Example Bad: Locked overlay until finished
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Autocomplete
entries.summary: Help users find results faster
entries.content:
No: 89
Category: Search
Issue: Autocomplete
Platform: Web
Description: Help users find results faster
Do: Show predictions as user types
Don't: Require full type and enter
Code Example Good: Debounced fetch + dropdown
Code Example Bad: No suggestions
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Reduced Motion
entries.summary: Respect user's motion preferences
entries.content:
No: 9
Category: Animation
Issue: Reduced Motion
Platform: All
Description: Respect user's motion preferences
Do: Check prefers-reduced-motion media query
Don't: Ignore accessibility motion settings
Code Example Good: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)
Code Example Bad: No motion query check
Severity: High

entries.title: No Results
entries.summary: Dead ends frustrate users
entries.content:
No: 90
Category: Search
Issue: No Results
Platform: Web
Description: Dead ends frustrate users
Do: Show 'No results' with suggestions
Don't: Blank screen or '0 results'
Code Example Good: Try searching for X instead
Code Example Bad: No results found.
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Bulk Actions
entries.summary: Editing one by one is tedious
entries.content:
No: 91
Category: Data Entry
Issue: Bulk Actions
Platform: Web
Description: Editing one by one is tedious
Do: Allow multi-select and bulk edit
Don't: Single row actions only
Code Example Good: Checkbox column + Action bar
Code Example Bad: Repeated actions per row
Severity: Low

entries.title: Disclaimer
entries.summary: Users need to know they talk to AI
entries.content:
No: 92
Category: AI Interaction
Issue: Disclaimer
Platform: All
Description: Users need to know they talk to AI
Do: Clearly label AI generated content
Don't: Present AI as human
Code Example Good: AI Assistant label
Code Example Bad: Fake human name without label
Severity: High

entries.title: Streaming
entries.summary: Waiting for full text is slow
entries.content:
No: 93
Category: AI Interaction
Issue: Streaming
Platform: All
Description: Waiting for full text is slow
Do: Stream text response token by token
Don't: Show loading spinner for 10s+
Code Example Good: Typewriter effect
Code Example Bad: Spinner until 100% complete
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Gaze Hover
entries.summary: Elements should respond to eye tracking before pinch
entries.content:
No: 94
Category: Spatial UI
Issue: Gaze Hover
Platform: VisionOS
Description: Elements should respond to eye tracking before pinch
Do: Scale/highlight element on look
Don't: Static element until pinch
Code Example Good: hoverEffect()
Code Example Bad: onTap only
Severity: High

entries.title: Depth Layering
entries.summary: UI needs Z-depth to separate content from environment
entries.content:
No: 95
Category: Spatial UI
Issue: Depth Layering
Platform: VisionOS
Description: UI needs Z-depth to separate content from environment
Do: Use glass material and z-offset
Don't: Flat opaque panels blocking view
Code Example Good: .glassBackgroundEffect()
Code Example Bad: bg-white
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Auto-Play Video
entries.summary: Autoplaying media consumes data and creates motion barriers
entries.content:
No: 96
Category: Sustainability
Issue: Auto-Play Video
Platform: Web
Description: Autoplaying media consumes data and creates motion barriers
Do: Prefer click-to-play; provide pause and captions; stop off-screen and honor reduced motion
Don't: Auto-play high-resolution loops without pause or captions
Code Example Good: <video controls preload="none"><track kind="captions" /></video>
Code Example Bad: autoplay loop
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Asset Weight
entries.summary: Heavy 3D/Image assets increase carbon footprint
entries.content:
No: 97
Category: Sustainability
Issue: Asset Weight
Platform: Web
Description: Heavy 3D/Image assets increase carbon footprint
Do: Compress and lazy load 3D models
Don't: Load 50MB textures
Code Example Good: Draco compression
Code Example Bad: Raw .obj files
Severity: Medium

entries.title: Feedback Loop
entries.summary: AI needs user feedback to improve
entries.content:
No: 98
Category: AI Interaction
Issue: Feedback Loop
Platform: All
Description: AI needs user feedback to improve
Do: Thumps up/down or 'Regenerate'
Don't: Static output only
Code Example Good: Feedback component
Code Example Bad: Read-only text
Severity: Low

entries.title: Motion Sensitivity
entries.summary: Parallax/Scroll-jacking causes nausea
entries.content:
No: 99
Category: Accessibility
Issue: Motion Sensitivity
Platform: All
Description: Parallax/Scroll-jacking causes nausea
Do: Honor prefers-reduced-motion and present the final readable state without parallax or scroll-jacking
Don't: Force scroll effects
Code Example Good: @media (prefers-reduced-motion)
Code Example Bad: ScrollTrigger.create()
Severity: High

entries.title: Overview
entries.summary: Community analysis of 1win. An analysis of 1win's design language — a near-black crypto casino and sportsbook built on Inter at heavy weights, where a vivid green action color and an electric blue secondary carry every CTA across dense, full-bleed game-tile rails, promo cards, and live betting panels on a flat dark-grey surface ladder.

## Overview

1win is a crypto casino and sportsbook that runs almost entirely on a near-black canvas (`{colors.canvas}` — #141415), a flat, slightly cool dark field that lets thousands of vibrant game thumbnails do the shouting. The chrome around the content is deliberately quiet: dark-grey surfaces (`{colors.surface}` — #2e3035), faint translucent hairlines, and off-white text (`{colors.ink}` — #f0f2f5). Against that restraint, two action colors carry the entire interactive layer — a vivid green (`{colors.primary}` — #00b24b) on the "Registration" CTA and every primary confirm, and an electric blue (`{colors.secondary}` — #0075ff) on "Log In", links, the "Show more" pill, active tabs, and bet highlights.

The layout is a high-density product surface, not a marketing page. A fixed left icon rail holds category navigation; the main column is a long stack of horizontally-scrolling rails — "Top games", "Slots", "Originals", game providers — each a row of full-bleed, brightly-illustrated `game-tile` thumbnails. Promotional bonuses ride in gradient-rich `hero-banner` cards at the top, and the sportsbook adds match rows with `bet-odds-button` chips and a right-hand `betslip-panel`. Typography is Inter set at heavy weights only (600 and 800) — even body copy is semibold — which gives the dense UI a punchy, app-like confidence rather than an editorial calm.

Color discipline is the key to reading this brand correctly: the loud purples, reds, ambers, and violets that fill the screen all live *inside* game artwork and bonus-card illustrations — they are content, not chrome. The system itself is monochrome dark plus exactly two signals: green for "go / win / register" and blue for "secondary / navigate / live". Everything structural is built from the dark surface ladder and those two accents.

**Key Characteristics:**
- Near-black `{colors.canvas}` foundation with a flat `{colors.surface}` card/tile ladder — depth comes from surface shifts and faint `{colors.hairline}` borders, not heavy shadow.
- Two-signal action system: green `{colors.primary}` for primary CTAs (Registration, confirm) and blue `{colors.secondary}` for secondary actions, links, and live/betting highlights.
- Inter at heavy weights only (600 / 800) — even `{typography.body}` is semibold, giving the dense UI an app-like punch.
- Content-forward game rails — full-bleed `game-tile` artwork supplies all the saturation; the surrounding frame stays monochrome dark.
- Pill language for badges and status (`{rounded.full}`), modest `{rounded.lg}`–`{rounded.xl}` on buttons, and `{rounded.card}` (16px) on tiles, promo cards, and panels.
- A left icon `sidebar-rail` + dense horizontally-scrolling rails define the shell, closer to a native app than a website.

## Colors

> Source pages analyzed: home, promotions, betting, vip-club.

### Brand & Accent
- **Action Green** (`{colors.primary}` — #00b24b): The primary action color — the "Registration" CTA, primary confirms, betslip place-bet, and section accent icons. The brand's "go / win" signal.
- **Electric Blue** (`{colors.secondary}` — #0075ff): The secondary action — "Log In", text links, the "Show more" pill, active tabs, badges, and live/betting highlights.
- **On Primary** (`{colors.on-primary}` — #ffffff): White text/icons on the green and blue fills.

### Surface
- **Canvas** (`{colors.canvas}` — #141415): The page background and the fill of the nav and `sidebar-rail` — a flat near-black.
- **Surface** (`{colors.surface}` — #2e3035): Cards, game tiles, promo cards, betslip panels, utility buttons, and input fields — the single elevated dark step.
- **Hairline** (`{colors.hairline}` — #2d2f33): The faint 1px divider/card border, a translucent cool-grey edge that reads against both canvas and surface.

### Text
- **Ink** (`{colors.ink}` — #f0f2f5): Primary text, the wordmark, and headings — a soft off-white.
- **Muted** (`{colors.muted}` — #9aa1b1): Secondary labels, inactive nav glyphs, footer text.
- **Faint** (`{colors.faint}` — #53575f): Tertiary/placeholder text and disabled labels.
- **Black** (`{colors.black}` — #000000): Maximum-contrast text used on the brightest accent fills and light promo surfaces.

## Typography

### Font Family
The entire system is set in **Inter** (`Inter, sans-serif`), and only at heavy weights — **600 (semibold)** and **800 (extrabold)**. There is no regular-weight body text; even running copy is semibold, which is what gives the dense, data-heavy interface its punchy, native-app feel. Headlines and bonus figures use 800; everything functional uses 600.

### Hierarchy

| Token | Size | Weight | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{typography.display}` | 33px | 800 | 1.1 | 0 | Hero / page headlines (bonus figures, "Promotions") |
| `{typography.heading}` | 20px | 800 | 1.2 | 0 | Section + card titles |
| `{typography.title}` | 16px | 600 | 1.3 | 0 | Game titles, row headers, outlined pills |
| `{typography.body}` | 14px | 600 | 1.4 | 0 | Default body, button labels |
| `{typography.ui}` | 13px | 600 | 1.3 | 0 | Inline UI text, odds, metadata |
| `{typography.caption}` | 12px | 600 | 1.3 | 0 | Badges, chips, micro-labels |

### Principles
Hierarchy is built from size and the 600↔800 weight jump, never from a light/regular contrast. The heavy floor keeps small UI text legible against the dark, busy backdrop and matches the high-energy gambling context.

### Note on Font Substitutes
Inter is an open-source Google Font, so no substitution is needed. If a fallback is required, any grotesque with a strong semibold (e.g. Manrope, Geist) preserves the heavy-weight character; keep body at 600+ to retain the app-like density.

## Layout

### Spacing System
- **Base unit**: 8px.
- **Tokens (front matter)**: `{spacing.xxs}` 2px · `{spacing.xs}` 4px · `{spacing.sm}` 8px · `{spacing.md}` 12px · `{spacing.lg}` 16px · `{spacing.xl}` 20px · `{spacing.xxl}` 24px · `{spacing.xxxl}` 32px
- Controls run tight — `{spacing.sm}`×`{spacing.md}` (8×12px) is the recurring button padding; cards and panels use `{spacing.lg}`–`{spacing.xxl}` (16–24px) interiors.

### Grid & Container
The shell is a fixed left icon `sidebar-rail` plus a fluid content column. Discovery uses horizontally-scrolling rails (carousels) of `game-tile` thumbnails rather than wrapping grids; the promotions page uses a 2-up card grid, and the sportsbook uses full-width match rows with a docked right-hand `betslip-panel`.

### Whitespace Philosophy
Density is the point — tiles pack close together to maximize the number of games in view, and the dark canvas itself does the separating between rails. Vertical gaps between labeled rails are modest; the brightness step between a tile and the canvas, plus a faint `{colors.hairline}`, supplies most of the structure.

### Responsive Strategy

#### Breakpoints
| Name | Width | Key Changes |
|---|---|---|
| Mobile | < 768px | Left rail collapses to a bottom/hamburger nav; rails shorten; betslip becomes a bottom sheet |
| Tablet | 768–1023px | Condensed rail; fewer tiles per rail; 2-up promo grid retained |
| Laptop | 1024–1439px | Full rail + multi-tile rails |
| Desktop | ≥ 1440px (up to 1920px) | Widest rails + persistent betslip panel |

#### Touch Targets
Buttons carry `{spacing.sm}`×`{spacing.md}` padding and pills clear comfortable tap sizes; the green `button-primary` is the largest, highest-priority tap surface. Aim for 44×44px minimum on the dense rails.

#### Collapsing Strategy
The left `sidebar-rail` collapses first (to a hamburger or bottom bar). Category tab strips and `bet-odds-button` rows become horizontally scrollable rather than wrapping. Game rails keep their carousel behavior at every width, simply showing fewer tiles. The `betslip-panel` docks to the right on desktop and becomes a bottom sheet on mobile.

#### Image Behavior
Game thumbnails are full-bleed inside `{rounded.card}` corners (no internal padding) in portrait-leaning and square ratios; the artwork supplies all the color. Promo cards carry edge-to-edge photography behind an `{colors.ink}` title. Tiles lazy-load as rails scroll into view, with the `{colors.surface}` tile color as the placeholder.

## Elevation & Depth

Depth is mostly tonal — a flat two-step surface ladder rather than layered shadows.

| Level | Treatment | Use |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `{colors.canvas}` flat | Page background, nav, sidebar rail |
| 1 | `{colors.surface}` + `{colors.hairline}` border | Cards, tiles, promo cards, betslip, buttons, inputs |
| Floating | `{colors.surface}` + soft `rgba(0,0,0,0.4)` shadow | Modals, dropdowns, the docked betslip lifted above content |

### Decorative Depth
The brand's visual richness comes from the game and promo artwork (radial-gradient bonus banners, illustrated tiles) layered on the flat dark canvas — not from UI shadows. Selected/active states use the green or blue accent as a glow-like emphasis rather than elevation.

## Shapes

### Border Radius Scale

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `{rounded.xs}` | 4px | Small chips, inner elements |
| `{rounded.sm}` | 6px | Compact cards, small media |
| `{rounded.md}` | 8px | Inputs, odds buttons, medium elements |
| `{rounded.lg}` | 10px | Primary / secondary / ghost buttons |
| `{rounded.xl}` | 12px | Utility buttons |
| `{rounded.card}` | 16px | Game tiles, promo cards, hero banners, panels |
| `{rounded.full}` | 999px | Pills, badges, avatars, circular controls |

### Photography Geometry
Game artwork is framed at `{rounded.card}` (16px) and runs full-bleed inside the tile. Promo cards use the same 16px frame with edge-to-edge imagery. Avatars, status badges, and provider chips use `{rounded.full}`. There is no exposed photography outside the gaming/promo content — the structural chrome stays geometric and flat.

## Components

> **No hover states documented.** Each spec covers Default and Active/Pressed only. Variants live as separate `components:` entries.

### Buttons

**`button-primary`** — the green "Registration" / primary-confirm CTA, the highest-visibility control.
- Background `{colors.primary}`, text `{colors.on-primary}`, type `{typography.body}`, rounded `{rounded.lg}`, padding `{spacing.sm}` `{spacing.md}` (8×12px).

**`button-secondary`** — the blue "Log In" / secondary action and the "Show more" pill.
- Background `{colors.secondary}`, text `{colors.on-primary}`, type `{typography.body}`, rounded `{rounded.lg}`, padding 8×12px.

**`button-tertiary`** — the dark-grey utility button ("More events", "Read more").
- Background `{colors.surface}`, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.body}`, rounded `{rounded.xl}`, padding 8×12px.

**`button-ghost`** — a low-emphasis grey control on dense rows.
- Background `{colors.surface}`, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.body}`, rounded `{rounded.lg}`, padding `0` `{spacing.sm}` (0×8px).

### Navigation

**`top-nav`** — the sticky header carrying the 1win wordmark, search, balance, and the green Registration + blue Log In CTAs.
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.ink}`, padding 8×16px, with a `{colors.hairline}` base edge.

**`sidebar-rail`** — the fixed left icon rail (Casino, Sports, categories).
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, glyphs `{colors.muted}`, padding `{spacing.sm}`. Active item marked in `{colors.primary}`.

### Inputs & Forms

**`text-input`** — search and betslip amount fields.
- Background `{colors.surface}`, text `{colors.ink}`, placeholder `{colors.faint}`, border `{colors.hairline}`, type `{typography.body}`, rounded `{rounded.md}`, padding 8×12px.

**`bet-odds-button`** — the odds chip in sportsbook match rows.
- Background `{colors.surface}`, text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.ui}`, rounded `{rounded.md}`, padding 8×12px. Selected state highlights in `{colors.secondary}`.

### Pills & Badges

**`pill-badge`** — the solid blue status/count badge.
- Background `{colors.secondary}`, text `{colors.on-primary}`, type `{typography.caption}`, rounded `{rounded.full}`, padding `0` `{spacing.xs}` (0×4px).

**`pill-outline`** — the bordered filter/category pill.
- Text `{colors.ink}`, type `{typography.title}`, rounded `{rounded.full}`, padding 0×8px, with a `{colors.hairline}` border.

### Cards & Containers

**`game-tile`** — the core discovery unit: a full-bleed game thumbnail.
- Background `{colors.surface}` (placeholder), rounded `{rounded.card}`. Artwork fills edge-to-edge with no padding.

**`hero-banner`** — the top welcome-bonus / promo banner.
- Background `{colors.surface}` with edge-to-edge gradient imagery, headline `{colors.ink}` in `{typography.display}`, rounded `{rounded.card}`, padding `{spacing.xxl}`.

**`promo-card`** — a promotions-page card (full-bleed photo + title + chips).
- Background `{colors.surface}`, title `{colors.ink}`, rounded `{rounded.card}`, padding `{spacing.lg}`.

**`feature-card`** — generic dark content card.
- Background `{colors.surface}`, text `{colors.ink}`, border `{colors.hairline}`, rounded `{rounded.card}`, padding `{spacing.lg}`.

**`feature-card-elevated`** — a feature card lifted above the page (floating shadow), base for modal/toast surfaces.
- Background `{colors.surface}`, text `{colors.ink}`, rounded `{rounded.card}`, padding `{spacing.lg}`, soft `rgba(0,0,0,0.4)` shadow.

**`betslip-panel`** — the docked sportsbook betslip / wheel-of-fortune panel.
- Background `{colors.surface}`, text `{colors.ink}`, rounded `{rounded.card}`, padding `{spacing.lg}`. Confirm action uses `button-primary`.

**`footer`** — the page footer (support, information, categories columns).
- Background `{colors.canvas}`, text `{colors.muted}`, headings `{colors.ink}`, padding `{spacing.xxl}`.

### Examples (illustrative)

> Kit-mirror demonstration surfaces. Each `ex-*` entry references 1win's brand-native primitives (`{colors.surface}`, `{colors.primary}`, `{rounded.card}`, the spacing scale) so downstream consumers re-skin the same 10 illustrative surfaces consistently. These are not extracted brand components.

**`ex-pricing-tier`** — Default Pricing tier card. Re-uses feature-card chrome with brand canvas-soft surface.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `textColor`, `borderColor`, `rounded`, `padding`

**`ex-pricing-tier-featured`** — Featured/highlighted tier — polarity-flipped surface (dark fill + light text in light mode, light fill + dark text in dark mode).
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `textColor`, `rounded`, `padding`

**`ex-product-selector`** — What's Included summary card — re-purposed for SaaS / B2B verticals (NOT a literal product gallery).
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`

**`ex-cart-drawer`** — Subscription summary — re-purposed for SaaS / B2B (line items per add-on, not literal cart).
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`, `item-divider`

**`ex-app-shell-row`** — Sidebar nav row inside the App Shell example. Active state uses brand primary as the indicator.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `activeIndicator`, `rounded`, `padding`

**`ex-data-table-cell`** — Default data-table th + td chrome. Header uses mono-caps eyebrow typography; body uses body-sm.
- Properties: `headerBackground`, `headerTypography`, `bodyTypography`, `cellPadding`, `rowBorder`

**`ex-auth-form-card`** — Sign-in / sign-up card. Re-uses feature-card chrome with text-input primitives inside.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`

**`ex-modal-card`** — Modal dialog surface — same chrome as feature-card with elevated shadow.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`

**`ex-empty-state-card`** — Empty-state illustration frame.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`, `captionTypography`

**`ex-toast`** — Toast notification surface — feature-card shape + medium shadow.
- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`, `typography`


## Do's and Don'ts

### Do
- Reserve `{colors.primary}` (green) for primary actions — Registration, confirm, place-bet — and `{colors.secondary}` (blue) for secondary actions, links, and live/betting highlights.
- Build depth with the surface ladder (`{colors.canvas}` → `{colors.surface}`) plus a faint `{colors.hairline}` edge; avoid heavy shadows.
- Set every label in Inter 600+ (`{typography.body}` / `{typography.caption}`); use the 800 weight for headlines and bonus figures.
- Let game and promo artwork supply the color — keep the surrounding chrome monochrome dark.
- Use `{rounded.lg}`–`{rounded.xl}` on buttons, `{rounded.card}` (16px) on tiles/cards/panels, and `{rounded.full}` on pills and badges.
- Pair accent fills with `{colors.on-primary}` (white) text for legibility.

### Don't
- Don't promote game-tile or bonus-banner gradient colors (the purples, reds, violets, ambers) into the UI palette — they are content, not chrome.
- Don't add a third structural accent; the system is green + blue only.
- Don't use pure-regular weights — there is no Inter 400 here; body copy is semibold.
- Don't pad game tiles — artwork is full-bleed inside `{rounded.card}` corners.
- Don't rely on drop shadows for elevation; the surface brightness step is the elevation language.

entries.title: Overview
entries.summary: Community analysis of airbnb. A warm, generous consumer marketplace anchored on a clean white canvas and Airbnb Rausch (#ff385c), the single brand voltage that carries every primary CTA, search-button orb, and rating dot. Type runs Airbnb Cereal VF at modest weights — display sits at 22–28px in weight 500/600 rather than the heavy 700+ that fintech and enterprise systems use; the brand trusts photography and generous whitespace over typographic muscle. Three product entries (Homes, Experiences, Services) sit in the top nav with hand-illustrated 32-icon glyphs and "NEW" badges, signaling a marketplace expansion rather than a feature dump. Pill-shaped search bars (`{rounded.full}`), softly rounded property cards (`{rounded.lg}` ~14px), and 32px button radii read as friendly and human — there is no hard corner anywhere except the body grid.
